text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING ALERT — p99 latency spike for customer QuantumLedger (VPC: ql-vpc-eu2). Metric: inference.p99 > 6s for 3 consecutive mins. Trigger: 2025-03-14T02:15:32Z. Link: https://redwood.monitor/q-ql-vpc-eu2/p99

sanjay: I'm the primary oncall, ack. jumping in. @maya @chris can you join?

maya: joining. pulling pool metrics and recent deploys now.

chris: looking at pool eu2-ql-pool-1 — GPU util ~60%, but queue depth spiked to 420 and avg kv-cache miss rate jumped to 78%. suspect KV cache thrashing for long-tail sequences.

elena: CSM Zoe says customer sees timeouts on admin portal and batch jobs failing. tagging @zoe-csm.

zoe-csm: Confirmed with QuantumLedger SRE — they started a heavy backfill at 02:05 UTC and are running many long-context evals against a LLM endpoint. They estimate ~3x baseline traffic. They asked for ETA.

nina: noted. Customer impact: p95 around 1.7s but p99 >6s and tail errors ~4%.

sanjay: quick runbook plan (vpc-tail-mitigation):
1) divert new sessions from ql-vpc-eu2 to fallback variant `redwood-ql-small` (lower memory, lower latency)
2) scale up dedicated nodes (+2 gpus) on eu2-pool ASAP
3) apply tenant throttling for top noisy tenants (hold connections)
4) if no improvement, initiate warm failover to eu1 standby region

chris: starting step1 — registering fallback route in router. command:```
POST /admin/routing
{ "vpc": "ql-vpc-eu2", "route": "fallback", "model": "redwood-ql-small", "condition": "new_sessions" }
```

maya: curl to control plane shows route applied, verifying at edge. logs:```
[02:19:41] route-change: ql-vpc-eu2 -> redwood-ql-small (new_sessions) by chris
[02:19:43] traffic-shift: ~12% of new sessions diverted
```

sanjay: good. moving to scale step2 — invoking autoscale override for pool eu2-ql-pool-1.

ops-bot: Runbook invoked: `vpc-tenant-isolation-v3` by sanjay. Incident ID INC-2025-QL-78.

ben: autoscale request sent:```
POST /infra/autoscale/override
{ "pool": "eu2-ql-pool-1", "delta_nodes": 2, "reason": "p99 spike QuantumLedger" }
```

maya: cloud provider shows two new instances provisioning (ETA ~3m). watching.

chris: while new nodes start, I'm seeing a small set of tenants within ql-vpc (tenant ids: t-197, t-203, t-42) contributing 65% of requests with long contexts. Recommend selective throttling on those tenants.

sanjay: agree. start soft throttles (rate limit to 60% of baseline) and let CSM coordinate messaging. command:```
POST /admin/vpc/ql-vpc-eu2/throttle
{ "tenants": ["t-197","t-203","t-42"], "rate": "0.6" }
```

nina: applied soft throttle. observing immediate queue depth drop to 180. p99 drops to ~3.2s (improvement).

zoe-csm: sending customer update: "We diverted new sessions to a low-latency model and applied temporary rate limits to the heaviest tenants to stabilize API. We're bringing additional capacity online. We expect restored latencies within 10 minutes."

sanjay: good customer comms. note: need to capture spike profile and save KV cache snapshots for debug. @chris can you export cache metrics and a sample of affected requests (sanitized)?

chris: exporting now. saved snapshot: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-2025-QL-78/cache-snap-0219.tar.gz. sample request IDs saved (sanitized): rq-5561, rq-5562, rq-5599.

ops-bot: New nodes are healthy and joined pool eu2-ql-pool-1. Autoscale event complete.

maya: after nodes came online and throttles applied, p99 stabilized at ~1.4s, tail errors down to 0.8%. Traffic back to normal shape.

sanjay: moving to containment->postmortem phase. Actions so far:
- diverted new sessions to `redwood-ql-small` (temporary fallback)
- +2 nodes added to eu2-ql-pool-1
- soft throttles applied to top noisy tenants t-197/t-203/t-42
- cache snapshots and request samples collected

ben: recommendation for next steps (post-incident):
- work with customer to reschedule heavy backfills to off-peak windows or use a dedicated batch cluster
- add automated detection for long-context KV thrash patterns and preemptive warming
- create a tenant-specific admission control policy to prevent a single tenant from exhausting KV cache

nina: logging a followup run: `INC-2025-QL-78 - customer stabilization & mitigation` with assigned owners: chris (root cause & replay), maya (runbooks + detection), zoe-csm (customer coordination).

zoe-csm: customer acknowledged and accepted throttling. They're running a toned-down backfill and will provide a replay plan.

sanjay: I'm marking incident as mitigated. We'll keep the thread open for postmortem notes and timeline. Closing actions: schedule 1h post-incident sync at 2025-03-14T04:00Z.

oncall-rotations-bot: Incident INC-2025-QL-78 status changed to MITIGATED by sanjay at 2025-03-14T02:35:12Z.

chris: note for postmortem — attach cache snapshot and edge logs, include BPF summary for kernel-level stalls.

maya: will draft runbook updates to include explicit fallback route testing and automated throttle thresholds.

zoe-csm: adding customer timeline to the PSR and sending a formal incident summary to QuantumLedger SRE.

sanjay: thanks all. good triage and fast execution. :thumbsup:
